<a id="netra-methods"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-01.svg" alt="Netra methods: Netra estimates how much of a company&#x27;s retired carbon credits likely represent real emission reductions. It is a risk estimate based on average research findings per project type, not a verdict on any single project or company." width="100%"></p>

<p align="center"><img src="assets/how-it-works.svg" alt="How Netra works in six steps" width="100%"></p>

<a id="data"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-02.svg" alt="Data: Retirements: Berkeley Voluntary Registry Offsets Database (VROD) v2026-08, registry files for Verra (VCS) and Gold Standard, retirements from 2020-01-01. 342,012 rows, 876.05 million tCO2e. License: CC BY 4.0. Owner: Verra Beneficial Owner and Gold Standard Using Entity, normalized (lowercase, punctuation and legal suffixes removed). 59.6% of retired tonnes name an owner. Blank and &quot;Not Applicable&quot; entries are grouped as &quot;(no owner listed)&quot;. ICVCM status: snapshot of https://icvcm.org/assessment-status/ (page modified 2026-08-18, retrieved 2026-10-20), 174 methodology rows, stored in dat" width="100%"></p>

<a id="outcome-achievement-ratio-oar"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-03.svg" alt="Outcome Achievement Ratio (OAR): OAR = share of issued credits that research estimates to be real reductions. Source: Probst et al. 2024, Nature Communications, doi:10.1038/s41467-024-53645-z (2,346 projects, about 1 billion tCO2e). Ranges are the paper&#x27;s central estimate minus and plus the weighted variance, from the Figure 4a source data (Supplementary Data 6), clipped to 0-100%. Category Central Range Notes Avoided deforestation (REDD+) 24.7% 0-96.7% Wide range; see also West et al. 2023, Science, doi:10.1126/science.ade3535 Cookstoves 10.8% 10.5-11.1% Consistent with Gill-Wiehl et al. 2024" width="100%"></p>

<a id="classification-rules-three-independent-signals"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-05.svg" alt="Classification rules (three independent signals): Every project gets a category only when independent sources agree. Any disagreement gets no OAR, so a dispute can only lower a company&#x27;s estimated real tonnes, never raise it. Berkeley VROD curated project Type (PROJECTS sheet, 11,856 projects), joined by project ID (Verra VCS&lt;id&gt;, Gold Standard GS&lt;GSID&gt;). Join rate: 100% of rows and tonnes. CarbonPlan OffsetsDB project_type (independent classification, parquet release; covers 78.2% of retired tonnes with a known type). Registry methodology code (REDD+: VM0004/6/7/9/15/37/48; biomass cookstoves" width="100%"></p>

<p align="center"><img src="assets/three-signals.svg" alt="Three-signal classification" width="100%"></p>

<a id="icvcm-status"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-06.svg" alt="ICVCM status: Each methodology string is matched to the ICVCM table by code and version range: approved (CCP-Approved, including conditional), not_approved (&quot;Does not meet&quot;), or not_assessed (not listed, under assessment, or version outside an assessed range). Examples: ACM0002 and AMS-I.D do not meet; GS TPDDTEC v2.0-3.1, VM0050, VM0048 and the GS metered methodology v1.0-1.2 are approved; legacy REDD+ methodologies VM0007, VM0009 and VM0015 are not listed. Share of retired tonnes since 2020: approved 4.5%, not approved 35.9%, not assessed 59.6%." width="100%"></p>

<a id="headline-numbers-vrod-v2026-08-verra-gold-since-2020"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-07.svg" alt="Headline numbers (VROD v2026-08, Verra + Gold, since 2020): Tonnes with a published OAR: 37.8%. Of those, likely real: 19.4% central (range 2.4-68.8%, driven mainly by REDD+ uncertainty). Largest single owner entry: &quot;Not Disclosed&quot;, 89.4 million t." width="100%"></p>

<p align="center"><img src="assets/key-findings.svg" alt="Key findings" width="100%"></p>

<a id="known-limits"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-08.svg" alt="Known limits: OAR values are averages per project type; individual projects vary widely. Categories without a published OAR (34.8% renewables, 26.8% other) cannot be scored and are reported separately. Owner names in registries do not always match the company making a claim (brokers, subsidiaries, brands)." width="100%"></p>

<a id="past-present-future"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-09.svg" alt="Past, present, future: Past to present: per-owner and market-wide yearly series (2020-2026). Market-wide, the likely-real share of OAR-covered tonnes stayed flat at 18-22% every year (2020: 18.7%, 2021: 22.4%, 2022: 18.0%, 2023: 20.2%, 2024: 18.0%, 2025: 17.9%, 2026 to Aug: 18.0%). Quality of what is retired has not improved. Present: each owner&#x27;s current mix, grade, ICVCM status share, and owner disclosure. Future: forward-looking flags already in the data: share of tonnes from methodologies ICVCM says do not meet the CCPs; ACM0002 and AMS-I.D will be inactivated as standalone methodologies i" width="100%"></p>

<a id="buyer-names"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-10.svg" alt="Buyer names: Registry beneficiary names are shown as published, with two repairs (clean_owner in pipeline/build.py): 4,560 names exported with Mac Roman mojibake (e.g. &quot;Societ√† Benefit&quot;) are decoded back to UTF-8 (&quot;Società Benefit&quot;), and statements such as &quot;Retired on behalf of easyJet for aviation emissions period ...&quot; are reduced to the named party (&quot;easyJet&quot;). Names are then normalized (case, punctuation, legal suffixes) to group retirements. Result: 44,546 buyers." width="100%"></p>

<a id="independent-emissions-climate-trace"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="assets/md/methods-11.svg" alt="Independent emissions (Climate TRACE): Source: Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory v5.7.0 (CC BY 4.0, https://zenodo.org/records/20830133), sector packages for fossil fuel operations, power, manufacturing and mineral extraction, gas co2e_100yr, year 2025, monthly source-level emissions summed per asset. Ownership: the packages&#x27; _emissions_sources_ownership_.csv files give each parent&#x27;s overall_share_percent per asset (the public API lists owners without shares, so it is not used for attribution). Attribution (pipeline/ownership.py): parent emissions = sum of asset emissions x known share. A pare" width="100%"></p>

<a id="buyer-classification"></a>
